name: Denver’s Peaceful Oasis for Travel Nurses & Nomads
description:
Enjoy the famous Colorado weather and unplug in indoor & outdoor living. Our charming cottage has a serene ambiance throughout every area.
Spend a sunny afternoon out in the garden hammock or garden parlor sofa, pr sink into the shared hot tub.
We are located next to downtown and in the neighborhood of lower highlands,
Superb coffee shops, restaurants, microbrews, distilleries, dispensaries & downtown. We are 420 outdoors only. LGBT Friendly, allergy-free, fragrance-free & pet-free.
neighborhood_overview: The cottage is located in the center of Lower Highlands (LOHI) next to the Navajo Street Arts District. Catch a show at the iconic Bug Theater. Wandering the neighborhood to discover breweries, distilleries and bars for local drinks, tuck into a family owned taqueria or explore more formal dinning experience. We are a vibrant neighborhood in Denver where you can see and do but just a quick walk thru the park to downtown, or a mile drive to RiNo. We are just 2.5 mile walk or dirve to Meow Wolf.
host_about:
We are artists and tinkerers.
 
We enjoy many activities here in Denver -  cooking, growing fruits and vegetables are some that we get to do here at the cottages along with mixed media projects and furniture building. 

We are always up to some new outdoor project when the Colorado weather permits and hunker down inside by the fire in the winter keeping our hands busy with knitting, card making or some other project we can dream up.   In fact the most recent outdoor project is for an outdoor parlor that will be winter friendly. 

Giovanni and I have grown in our collaborations and embrace our age and abilities  for self governance in employment - Giovanni had moved into documentaries and I have been spending more time in the commercial film community. 

We have been in the lower highlands for over a decade now and have marveled in the changing landscape and exciting times for new restaurants, breweries and galleries.  We still love to take advantage of the great walks thru the neighborhood and down by the river as often as we can.

description: This impeccably remodeled 1930's charmer is located in one of Denver's most coveted neighborhoods, Wash Park West.  Awesome location, $5 Uber to Downtown, the Convention Center, Cherry Creek - Walking distance to Wash Park (Denver's most popular park) and the Cherry Creek bike trail. neighborhood_overview:
The Vibe: Local spots where urbanites and nearby residents—mostly 20- and 30-something renters, young-families, and homeowners—hang; foodies visiting the hood’s rich and varied selection of eateries; joggers finishing their loop at the adjacent Wash Park.

Grub: Head to the French-inspired Vert Kitchen for homemade sandwiches (try the curried chicken), or a fast-casual brunch. (Or not so casual: They also sell bottles of champagne.) For Greek food—a genre that’s a little sparse in Denver—Pete’s Central One is a mainstay. Wash Park West is also a great destination for Asian cuisine, and Thai Basil, although a chain, serves up the best green curry in that neighborhood. Next door, Fontana Sushi rolls up creative specials, like the Spiderman, which adds extra crab, spicy mayo, and eel sauce to the already scrumptious Spider roll.

name: GARDEN SUITE: COMFORT & BEAUTY IN AN HISTORIC HOME
description:
THE BEAUTIFUL, UPDATED Garden Suite is a perfect retreat for a traveler, parent, doctor/ intern, or an executive. It is private, secure & well managed, with 2 private entries. Nestled in our 1912 Arts and Crafts home, this apartment is open & spacious with comfy, elegant furnishings. A gas stove in the living room warms up wintry evenings.
We are a mature couple preferring a tranquil environment, so we seek an individual who shares these values. All is provided -Just bring a suitcase!
neighborhood_overview:
We are 10 minutes due east of downtown traveling by car on 17th Street. Directly to the west is the lovely Johnson and Wales campus just two blocks away, and Park Hill, one of Denver's oldest and most elegant neighborhoods is also to the west. Park Hill features some lovely parkways, including 17th Street, Montview Boulevard, 23rd Street and Monaco Boulevard; it is a nice place to walk. (And if you're really motivated, the Zoo, City Park and Museum of Nature and Science are about 2.5 miles west.)
To the north and south are the relatively newer neighborhoods of Stapleton and Lowry, with town centers, restaurants and cafes.
Going to the east, the neighborhoods are more transitional, but changing fast as they are now anchored by the newer and huge Anshutz Medical Campus. Not to be missed is the spanking new Stanley Marketplace, housed in a former airplane factory, with brewpubs and some of the most innovative new restaurants in Denver. I-70, the main route to the mountains
host_about:
Hello, thanks for taking the time to read about us.  I came from the beautiful Finger Lakes area in upstate New York, moving here at 18 years old because I "had never known until I came to Colorado that the sun could come out in winter. "  That being the case, of course I never left. Lynne is from Colorado, with great-grandparents who grew up in Georgetown and old Snowmass. Life back then was not glamorous and a living was cobbled together from gritty pursuits such as silver mining.  
We love beautiful spaces, the outdoors, art in its many forms, and the company of good friends.  One of our careers together has been restoring neglected historic homes, and our home has been an almost two-decades long work in progress.  Restoring the apartment was one of our earlier efforts, and as is usually the case, we found architectural clues as to what our home's earlier owners had been up to.  (Such as the enormous beams that proved the claim that our house had been moved from Denver Municipal Airport in 1928. That airport became the old Stapleton Airport. We also heard from a gentleman in his ninties that he had watched it being moved.)
We believe historic homes are living history, in real time.  Having modern amenities makes them all the more appealing.
Possibly our greatest love is travel.  We agree with St. Gus, who said "The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page." And of course our favorite part of traveling is and always will be connecting with people from all walks of life, from all around the world. We're so thankful to have the opportunity to do this once more through hosting. 
Wishing you safe and happy travels!

neighborhood_overview:
The property is located in one of the oldest neighborhoods in Denver - at edges of the Curtis Park, San Rafael and Clements Historic Districts - all of which are dominated by beautifully restored Victorian 1880's homes.

Clements Historic District typifies high-style Queen Anne and Italianate architecture, and is one of the most intact collections of late 19th Century Victorian high-style residential architecture in Denver. It is representative of the City’s rapid growth and middle class population of the 19th Century. The district maintains beautiful views of the Rocky Mountains to the west.

Curtis Park, Denver’s first street car suburb, is one of the city’s oldest and most diverse residential areas. The neighborhood’s heyday was from the late 1870s until 1893. The district is a showcase of architectural styles from that era, including Italianate, Eastlake, Queen Anne, and Victorian eclectic homes. Get a taste of Victorian Denver in a living room with preserved brick walls, stained glass and tall windows allowing lots of light. Rooms have high ceilings in this townhouse and are tied together with restored hardwood floors and original millwork.

City of Denver License # 2018-BFN-0004619

High ceilings, exposed brick walls, decorative trim and other elements make this original Victorian townhome a rare gem in a newly redeveloped neighborhood. The home is split level with the living room, dining room and kitchen downstairs and the bedrooms, office and bathroom upstairs. (Please note, guests with children should take extra precautions with the hardwood stairs.) Lots of natural light pours in through large windows and a patio is available for lounging in the back. There’s a 55” television in the living room and a 42” tv in the master bedroom. Granite counter tops and stainless appliances adorn the kitchen.

Guests have access to all areas accept the outdo
neighborhood_overview: The townhouse is in LoHi (Lower Highlands), a popular neighborhood due to its walking proximity to award-winning restaurants, breweries, and boutiques. Downtown Denver, Union Station, and Coors Field are just beyond the Highlands footbridge.

neighborhood_overview:
The house is on the popular “South Broadway” which hosts a ton of restaurants, bars, breweries, dispensary’s, and liquor stores all within walking distance. Awesome neighborhood with a TON to offer.

LOCALS KNOW:
Denver’s South Broadway neighborhood, affectionately known as SoBo, has grown from a major artery into downtown to an eclectic and funky mix of taverns, clothing stores, unique eateries, bookstores and hip, live music venues with rainbow crosswalks and dedicated bike lanes. From craft breweries, distilleries and cideries to sundrenched, rooftop patios, South Broadway thrives on the unique energy of its residents and visitors.

Home to Antique Row, South Broadway is not only a destination for pieces from the 17th century, but also for immersive art experiences at vibrant, independent galleries. Check out Turn of the Century Antiques for dolls and toys and Spectra Art Space for contemporary art pieces in a fun, welcoming environment.

description:
Superb basement apartment retreat in a classic home centered in a prime city location!

By day, experience authentic Denver with easy access to unique restaurants, museums, parks and tons of local favorites – all within minutes. Or, venture into the Rocky Mountains for world-famous skiing/snowboarding, climbing, biking, hiking or rafting in Colorado nature.

It's a perfect blend of urban vibrancy and relaxing space. And, one of our favorite parts about living here is what's nearby. For example:

- 2 blocks to a huge park with a lake and big ol' trees (walking trails, tennis courts, fishing, etc.)
- 2 to 7 minutes to four areas hugely popular with Denverites for dining, nightlife, breweries, art, shopping and culture (Tennyson, Highlands Square, LoHi and RiNo)
- 3 minutes to Regis University; 8 minutes to the Auraria campus (Metro State, CU Denver and CC of Denver); 14 minutes to the University of Denver; 26 minutes to the University of Colorado
- 5 to 15 minutes to nearly all of Denver's concert venues
- 7 to 10 minutes to watch any of our four major sports teams (Broncos, Rockies, Nuggets, Avalanche)
- 8 minutes to Union Station (Denver'
host_about:
Carolyn and I love Denver and Colorado entirely, and have lived here for years (I'm a native!) At home in our state, we thrive on art galleries, unique restaurants, mountain views, and fresh-powder skiing with a little organic gardening on the side.

When not at home, we absolutely love to travel and some of our favorite experiences have been diving in Bonaire, wine in Tuscany, or climbing the Acropolis in Athens. We're always looking for a new adventure!

Since we travel so much (and have stayed at a good chunk of Airbnbs ourselves), we like to put the knowledge of what we loved or what drove us nuts into our own Airbnb to make a space that's fantastic for our fellow travelers. We hope you love it!

neighborhood_overview: West Washington Park: This petite neighborhood is considered one of Denver’s most livable spaces. The area has a bubble effect—it sits barely south of Baker’s booming neighborhood and South Broadway dives, west of the ever-busy Washington Park, and walking distance to South Pearl Street, but maintains the air of quiet suburbia perfectly suited for families and professionals. Colloquially known as West Wash Park, the neighborhood is heavily residential, filled with early-20th century houses that have been turned into multi-unit rentals, and offers easy access to a variety of essential and just-for-fun amenities. (Think: grocery stores and fitness clubs, and watering holes and music venues.) Whether you’re a city dweller searching for a new date-night spot, or a Sunday volleyball player looking for a new place to fuel up and wind down after summer games, this residential stalwart offers many fun ways to recharge your routine.

The Capitol Hill Mansion Bed and Breakfast Inn has been in operation for approximately two decades and is the Number 1 rated bed and breakfast in Denver. The Mansion has a perfect 5.0 star average review on TripAdvisor with over 1000 reviews.

The owner, Carl, is a well known Gourmet chef, featured in Nationwide B&B cookbooks, and each morning he provides his guests with a true culinary experience. His rooms are constantly updated while retaining old world charm that rival the best hotels.
neighborhood_overview: The mansion is a Denver and National Landmark and has been given historic designation from the Landmark Preservation Commission, Colorado State Register of Historic Properties and the National Register of Historic Places. The mansion is within four (4) blocks of the State of Colorado Capital building, three (3) blocks to the History Colorado Museum, four (4) blocks to the Denver Art Museum, (1) block to the Molly Brown House Museum, and (2) blocks to the Vance Kirkland Museum, known as the “Museum District” and (5) blocks to the 16th Street mall and many other area attractions.
host_about:
Nestled in the quaint Capitol Hill Neighborhood of downtown Denver, this romantic Bed and Breakfast is a Colorado and National Historic Landmark and is just a short walk from everything in the Mile-High City, including attractions, gourmet restaurants, theaters, museums and shopping.

Built in 1891, the gorgeous ruby sandstone mansion is located on Denver’s famous “Millionaires Row,” just a block from the mansion immortalized in folklore -- the home of “Unsinkable Molly Brown.” This was Denver’s original upscale neighborhood. The homes here feature a variety of classical architectural styles, each with its own flamboyant and whimsical touches such as turrets, spires, and porches.

Eight elegantly appointed rooms and suites offer turn-of-the-century opulence with modern day flair.

host_about:
I am an entrepreneur (KalenJesse.com), entrepreneurial ecosystem builder, natural organizer, community builder and human-focused professional. I've supported hundreds of underrepresented entrepreneurs in starting and scaling their businesses. I am motivated by empowering others to empower themselves to create positive impact with their unique powers. 

I am a globally-minded professional with a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) focused in International Affairs/Political Anthropology, Spanish from Colorado College. MBA Candidate at CU Denver. I am a passionate mountain lover, deep sea diver, photographer, and life explorer in the heart of Denver. When I am not getting lost in nature with my camera, you might find me creatively cooking up some meals in the kitchen with no recipes in sight. I live for meeting great people, eating savory food, adventuring with no agenda,  learning from others' stories and amazing places.
 
I was born and raised in Denver, spent most of the last decade in New Zealand and now live back in my hometown. I take full advantage of my backyard by hiking, camping and skiing. In town, I venture out to live music, local bars, yoga and dance classes, photo galleries and supporting independent shops and restaurants. 
 
This private flat is an urban sanctuary in the heart of Denver - a place to regroup and rejuvenate with lots of activities and delicious restaurants within walking distance. I am excited to host fellow adventurers, families, and friends and offer what so many people offered me while living abroad. 

Safe Travels x
Kalen

 
 

My Place and Neighborhood:

My place is a comfortable, modern and safe abode in the heart of Denver's most colorful urban  neighborhood! You will have the entire unit to yourselves- queen bed, king bed, and  there is a comfortable sleepable futon couch in the living room, private bath and large and well-stocked kitchen.  The fireplace is a bonus in the winter months.

From the front door, you can take long or short walks admiring the historic Victorian bungalows and Arts and Crafts homes, gardens, and parks. There are quaint pockets of older retail areas with cafes, flower shops, and salons. On Colfax you’ll find a varied mix of coffee shops, restaurants, bars, music venues, yoga studios, cycling classes, film and record stores, and The Tattered Cover—a large locally-owned bookstore in a converted movie theater. You’ll also find tattoo parlors, photo-worthy graffiti walls, and plenty of gritty urban characters. As a photographer, my community never gets boring to document! You are just  a few blocks away from beautiful City Park with ponds and trails, the Denver Zoo, the Museum of Nature and Science, and the free Sunday “Jazz in the Park” concerts during summer months. Walk to the Esplanade Farmers Market on Sunday mornings June-October (E Colfax and Columbine St). It’s a wonderful neighborhood where just about anyone can find something to love.

The neighborhood was founded in the late 19th century and has retained much of its historic character, with many of its original buildings still standing. The neighborhood was founded in the late 19th century and has retained much of its historic character, with many of its original buildings still standing. Baker is home to a diverse community of artists, musicians, and creatives, and is known for its many galleries, studios, and performance spaces. ***About my house***
I try and filter through people to create the perfect mountain vibe and energy for my home which I bought and remodeled last year.  I am now pursuing a longtime dream of creating a mature Hostel, happy and full of energy with like-minded and adventurous, traveling spirits. Bed & Community Breakfast is what I'm trying to get to,...for now, its just a house full of fun people that commonly make dinner together, share smiles, and exchange stories and laughter.

My house is a nice home on peak 7, in Breckenridge.  It is over 2000 sq feet with up to 4 private bedrooms listed at a time.

***About my town***
Last winter, I was asked by a guest about my town and what I loved about it. She also wanted to know how I felt about Vail, and Utah. This was my response:

"Breck is definitely where its at as far as visiting and/or moving to. I moved here the day I graduated college and have never looked back. I just bought a home, and I am doing a full gut and extensive remodel just down the street. The mentality and way of life here is what I've fallen in love with. People work to live, not live to work. We focus our lives around being and playing outside (we have over 300 days of sunshine a year), everywhere is dog friendly, marijuanna is legal, (which speaks of the open mindness more than anything), and normally the talk around the table is about everyones previous or next travel adventure. Progression, love, empathy, and being and creating an overall sense of happiness is what my friends, and my town are all about. You get a local feel of warmth, community, and friendliness which is unlike any other resort community I've visited (which is many). Most resorts, especially those owned by Vail, do not cater to the community vibe, and most residents are only part-time 2nd and 3rd home owners. Vail is identical to a European ski resort. It was made to mock both architecture and community layout. And, the whole town is in a valley with I-70 running thru it! Utah is a far less progressive state than Colorado.

Once again, thank you for your time, energy, and consideration. I hope you get the best ski vacation any of us could ever manifest, with or without a stay in my home (((<3)))

Barnum sold as much of Barnum as possible before disposing of the remainder to his daughter, Helen Buchtel, for the price of one dollar. The district's interesting blend of urban charm and unique industrial revival makes it a great destination for visitors. Historic warehouses and factories now house jazz bars, restaurants, brewpubs, art galleries and working studios. The art definitely extends beyond gallery walls in this neighborhood, with its colorful and innovative street art murals in alleys and on buildings around almost every corner!

In 1878, the American circus mogul P.T. Barnum of the Barnum and Bailey Circus bought 760 acres for just $11,000, and a few years later, the Barnum subdivision was platted.

Barnum's involvement with his namesake's development has become part of Denver folklore, especially in the durable legend of the showman's plan to establish a winter home for his circus in the city. In fact, Barnum never wintered his animals anywhere other than Connecticut or Florida, and the entertainment entrepreneur made just four documented trips to Colorado. Barnum sold as much of Barnum as possible before disposing of the remainder to his daughter, Helen Buchtel, for the price of one dollar. host_about:
Pat's a Jersey Girl and Cindy is a Canadian who moved to Los Angeles 30 years ago to pursue her dream.  We now live in both Jersey AND L.A. -- and often Atlanta due to Cindy's work.  We like to say we are bi-coastal (sounds impressive, doesn't it?  ha-ha) When we are both out of Cali for work , we list our Silver Lake apartment on Airbnb.   The Salty V at the Shore is so big, it seemed a waste not to share, so we are listing rooms this summer for the first time.   

We love hosting our Airbnb travelers and knowing our home is well taken care of.  We are going on our 7th year as hosts and it's been a great experience.   
For some reason, we love living in tourist locations. Maybe its because we love hosting friends and family- including our AirBnb family-- as well as exploring the places around us.  OK, we moved to the Jersey Shore for the beach and the food-- there, we said it.  Oh- and we love to gamble. Yeah, that too.  Nothing beats L.A., tho, for the weather and the chill vibe- even in traffic. We love it there too.

We have two fur babies- Nina, our Chi mix, barks too much protecting the perimeter--we are working on that. You can never meet a more friendly dog, tho.  She is the darling of the dog beach.  Our kitty cat Harper Lee is one big sweetie, but shy. You won't see her around much. 

Pat likes to cook and host and hold babies- a natural caretaker.  She also loves the outdoors: camping, swimming, hiking and gardening.  She volunteers when she can-- for animals, people and political causes-tho we won't say which ones :o) 

Cindy,  loves everything about LA, especially the Dodgers.  She has a great deal of knowledge about the city and would be happy to pass along any information to help our guests enjoy their stay there. Cindy works as a TV/Film editor and loves watching TV and going to the movies, of course! 

We are a team, but Pat is usually the one you will talk to when you contact us, and Cindy is the city info expert and technical adviser (if you need to know how to work the remotes, tee-hee).  We are both a phone call or text away for anything you might need (including emergency toilet paper.) Yikes! 

We welcome our guests to enjoy our spaces and hope you are as comfortable as we are.  If there is anything at all we can do for you, just let us know.  We are happy when you are happy.

Pat's a Jersey Girl and Cindy is a Canadian who moved to Los Angeles 30 years ago to pursue her dream.  We now live in both Jersey AND L.A. -- and often Atlanta due to Cindy's work.  We like to say we are bi-coastal (sounds impressive, doesn't it?  ha-ha) When we are both out of Cali for work , we list our Silver Lake apartment on Airbnb. We love hosting our Airbnb travelers and knowing our home is well taken care of.  We are going on our 7th year as hosts and it's been a great experience.   
For some reason, we love living in tourist locations. Maybe its because we love hosting friends and family- including our AirBnb family-- as well as exploring the places around us.  OK, we moved to the Jersey Shore for the beach and the food-- there, we said it.  Oh- and we love to gamble. Yeah, that too.  Nothing beats L.A., tho, for the weather and the chill vibe- even in traffic. We love it there too.

We have two fur babies- Nina, our Chi mix, barks too much protecting the perimeter--we are working on that. You can never meet a more friendly dog, tho.  She is the darling of the dog beach.  Our kitty cat Harper Lee is one big sweetie, but shy. You won't see her around much. 

Pat likes to cook and host and hold babies- a natural caretaker.  She also loves the outdoors: camping, swimming, hiking and gardening.  She volunteers when she can-- for animals, people and political causes-tho we won't say which ones :o) 

Cindy,  loves everything about LA, especially the Dodgers.  She has a great deal of knowledge about the city and would be happy to pass along any information to help our guests enjoy their stay there. Cindy works as a TV/Film editor and loves watching TV and going to the movies, of course! 

We are a team, but Pat is usually the one you will talk to when you contact us, and Cindy is the city info expert and technical adviser (if you need to know how to work the remotes, tee-hee). neighborhood_overview:
What's To Love About Park Hill

Designed to showcase Mayor Speer's City Beautiful program, Park Hill, located on high ground east of City Park, remains one of the most coveted neighborhoods in Denver. Shaded by stately American Elms, Park Hill's exquisite thoroughfares: 17th Avenue, Forest, and Montview parkways, are among the most beautiful in the city.

In addition to an abundance of mature trees, 17th Avenue Parkway, designed by noted landscape architect Fredrick Law Olmsted, boasts a lush landscaped median and generous setbacks. Many of the neighborhood's first residences were designed by Fisher and Fisher, for decades one of the most distinguished architectural firms in Denver.

Early on, commentators raved that the thoroughfares of Park Hill -- "the most desirable residence portion of the city" -- rivaled Riverside Drive in New York, the Auteil and Passy in Paris, and Mayfair in London. Several of Denver's most beautiful churches are also found here.

With an emphasis on green design, our rooms at The Queen Anne provide both stylish comfort and eco-sensitivity. While staying with us, you can expect to find everything needed to make your room a home away from home. You won’t want to leave this charming, one-of-a-kind place.
The private deck at The Rooftop Room has a view of the city skyline, a glimpse of the mountains, and a private two person hot tub. The Rooftop room is furnished with a Queen size bed, tv, shower and a private work station.
neighborhood_overview: We are located on the eastern edge of Downtown Denver, about 7 blocks from the 16th St. Mall, and about 1 mile from Union Station. There is a small park, Benedict Fountain Park, across the street from the B&B. We are a short walk (4 blocks) from many excellent restaurants and bars in the Uptown District on 17th St. The State Capitol is about a 15 minute walk from the B&B and the Denver Art Museum and History Colorado Center are 1 mile south of us. The Denver Botanic Gardens are 2 miles southeast of us and the Denver Museum of Nature and Science is 2.5 miles to the east.
host_about: Welcome to our quiet, urban oasis in the heart of Downtown Denver, where historical architecture breathes new life. The Queen Anne Bed and Breakfast is a refreshing blend of innovative design with the environment and local community in mind.

description:

host_about:
Hi! I'm a small business owner and Summit County local for 15 years now! I'm a 37 year old adventurous and seeking spirit. Playing outside and being in the bright warm sun is my jam. I love dancing to live music, traveling, rock climbing, snowboarding, enlightenment, coffee, festivals and good conversation. 

My passion is cultivating connection both thru my home and work. I offer international retreats and teach others how to heal, transform, and root their lives in gratitude and compassion. I am a Medicine Woman and love to introduce a bridge to 5th dimensional living thru plant medicine and intuitive creation. You can find out more about me by searching Meg Richmond Medicine Woman. 

Currently, I am birthing a psychedelic community resource center with some of the greatest people on the planet, here is Colorado. Check out the Plant Magic Cafe- it’s out coffee shop gateway. And an up and coming 10 bed retreat center and ceremony space. Please stay with us here before/after visiting my home in breck. 

Additionally, I’m partnering with my best friend to develop our farm into a Net Positive Community. We are at the drawing board with engineers and surveyors to take conscious community to the next level on 38 acres We own in a nearby mountain town :) check out Salida, Colorado if you’re looking for a gem. 

Can't wait to meet you :) excited to host your body with my warm and comfy home and enchant your spirit. Thank you for your consideration!!!

***About my house***
I try and filter through people to create the perfect mountain vibe and energy for my home which I bought and remodeled last year.  I am now pursuing a longtime dream of creating a mature Hostel, happy and full of energy with like-minded and adventurous, traveling spirits. Bed & Community Breakfast is what I'm trying to get to,...for now, its just a house full of fun people that commonly make dinner together, share smiles, and exchange stories and laughter.

My house is a nice home on peak 7, in Breckenridge.  It is over 2000 sq feet with up to 4 private bedrooms listed at a time.

***About my town***
Last winter, I was asked by a guest about my town and what I loved about it. She also wanted to know how I felt about Vail, and Utah. This was my response:

"Breck is definitely where its at as far as visiting and/or moving to. I moved here the day I graduated college and have never looked back. I just bought a home, and I am doing a full gut and extensive remodel just down the street. The mentality and way of life here is what I've fallen in love with. People work to live, not live to work. We focus our lives around being and playing outside (we have over 300 days of sunshine a year), everywhere is dog friendly, marijuanna is legal, (which speaks of the open mindness more than anything), and normally the talk around the table is about everyones previous or next travel adventure. Progression, love, empathy, and being and creating an overall sense of happiness is what my friends, and my town are all about. You get a local feel of warmth, community, and friendliness which is unlike any other resort community I've visited (which is many). Most resorts, especially those owned by Vail, do not cater to the community vibe, and most residents are only part-time 2nd and 3rd home owners. Vail is identical to a European ski resort. It was made to mock both architecture and community layout. And, the whole town is in a valley with I-70 running thru it! Utah is a far less progressive state than Colorado.

Once again, thank you for your time, energy, and consideration. I hope you get the best ski vacation any of us could ever manifest, with or without a stay in my home (((<3)))

host_about:
Hi! I'm a small business owner and Summit County local for 15 years now! I'm a 37 year old adventurous and seeking spirit. Playing outside and being in the bright warm sun is my jam. I love dancing to live music, traveling, rock climbing, snowboarding, enlightenment, coffee, festivals and good conversation. 

My passion is cultivating connection both thru my home and work. I offer international retreats and teach others how to heal, transform, and root their lives in gratitude and compassion. I am a Medicine Woman and love to introduce a bridge to 5th dimensional living thru plant medicine and intuitive creation. You can find out more about me by searching Meg Richmond Medicine Woman. 

Currently, I am birthing a psychedelic community resource center with some of the greatest people on the planet, here is Colorado. Check out the Plant Magic Cafe- it’s out coffee shop gateway. And an up and coming 10 bed retreat center and ceremony space. Please stay with us here before/after visiting my home in breck. 

Additionally, I’m partnering with my best friend to develop our farm into a Net Positive Community. We are at the drawing board with engineers and surveyors to take conscious community to the next level on 38 acres We own in a nearby mountain town :) check out Salida, Colorado if you’re looking for a gem. 

Can't wait to meet you :) excited to host your body with my warm and comfy home and enchant your spirit. Thank you for your consideration!!!

***About my house***
I try and filter through people to create the perfect mountain vibe and energy for my home which I bought and remodeled last year.  I am now pursuing a longtime dream of creating a mature Hostel, happy and full of energy with like-minded and adventurous, traveling spirits. Bed & Community Breakfast is what I'm trying to get to,...for now, its just a house full of fun people that commonly make dinner together, share smiles, and exchange stories and laughter.

My house is a nice home on peak 7, in Breckenridge.  It is over 2000 sq feet with up to 4 private bedrooms listed at a time.

***About my town***
Last winter, I was asked by a guest about my town and what I loved about it. She also wanted to know how I felt about Vail, and Utah. This was my response:

"Breck is definitely where its at as far as visiting and/or moving to. I moved here the day I graduated college and have never looked back. I just bought a home, and I am doing a full gut and extensive remodel just down the street. The mentality and way of life here is what I've fallen in love with. People work to live, not live to work. We focus our lives around being and playing outside (we have over 300 days of sunshine a year), everywhere is dog friendly, marijuanna is legal, (which speaks of the open mindness more than anything), and normally the talk around the table is about everyones previous or next travel adventure. Progression, love, empathy, and being and creating an overall sense of happiness is what my friends, and my town are all about. You get a local feel of warmth, community, and friendliness which is unlike any other resort community I've visited (which is many). Most resorts, especially those owned by Vail, do not cater to the community vibe, and most residents are only part-time 2nd and 3rd home owners. Vail is identical to a European ski resort. It was made to mock both architecture and community layout. And, the whole town is in a valley with I-70 running thru it! Utah is a far less progressive state than Colorado.

Once again, thank you for your time, energy, and consideration. I hope you get the best ski vacation any of us could ever manifest, with or without a stay in my home (((<3)))

This site is not only the birthplace of Denver, dating back to an 1858 gold rush encampment, but also serves as a vibrant recreational hub today. The park features a kayak course, trails, and a grassy amphitheater for various community events. 2 pedestrian bridges connect park pathways, including Denver’s oldest metal bridge from 1888, offering views of both the city skyline and the riverfront.

neighborhood_overview:
Sunnyside is a neighborhood in Denver, Colorado, located on the city's north side. It's known for its mix of historic and modern homes, tree-lined streets, and a strong sense of community.

Sunnyside is known for its friendly and eclectic atmosphere. The neighborhood is very walkable, with tree-lined streets, welcoming front porches, and numerous parks.

Numerous local businesses, including restaurants, coffee shops, breweries, and more, are located throughout the neighborhood, primarily on 38th, 44th, and Tejon.

Community events such as the Sunnyside Music Festival in September add to the neighborhood's vibrant spirit.

The Sunnyside neighborhood is bounded by the Union Pacific Railroad lines to the east, I-70 to the north, Federal Boulevard to the west, and 38th Avenue to the south.

You can get a lovely view of the city by taking a short walk to Ciancio Park.

I am a Medicine Woman and love to introduce a bridge to 5th dimensional living thru plant medicine and intuitive creation. You can find out more about me by searching Meg Richmond Medicine Woman. 

Currently, I am birthing a psychedelic community resource center with some of the greatest people on the planet, here is Colorado. Check out the Plant Magic Cafe- it’s out coffee shop gateway. And an up and coming 10 bed retreat center and ceremony space. Please stay with us here before/after visiting my home in breck. 

Additionally, I’m partnering with my best friend to develop our farm into a Net Positive Community. We are at the drawing board with engineers and surveyors to take conscious community to the next level on 38 acres We own in a nearby mountain town :) check out Salida, Colorado if you’re looking for a gem. 

Can't wait to meet you :) excited to host your body with my warm and comfy home and enchant your spirit. Thank you for your consideration!!!

***About my house***
I try and filter through people to create the perfect mountain vibe and energy for my home which I bought and remodeled last year.  I am now pursuing a longtime dream of creating a mature Hostel, happy and full of energy with like-minded and adventurous, traveling spirits. Bed & Community Breakfast is what I'm trying to get to,...for now, its just a house full of fun people that commonly make dinner together, share smiles, and exchange stories and laughter.

My house is a nice home on peak 7, in Breckenridge.  It is over 2000 sq feet with up to 4 private bedrooms listed at a time.

***About my town***
Last winter, I was asked by a guest about my town and what I loved about it. She also wanted to know how I felt about Vail, and Utah. This was my response:

"Breck is definitely where its at as far as visiting and/or moving to. I moved here the day I graduated college and have never looked back. I just bought a home, and I am doing a full gut and extensive remodel just down the street. The mentality and way of life here is what I've fallen in love with. People work to live, not live to work. We focus our lives around being and playing outside (we have over 300 days of sunshine a year), everywhere is dog friendly, marijuanna is legal, (which speaks of the open mindness more than anything), and normally the talk around the table is about everyones previous or next travel adventure. Progression, love, empathy, and being and creating an overall sense of happiness is what my friends, and my town are all about. You get a local feel of warmth, community, and friendliness which is unlike any other resort community I've visited (which is many). Most resorts, especially those owned by Vail, do not cater to the community vibe, and most residents are only part-time 2nd and 3rd home owners. Vail is identical to a European ski resort. It was made to mock both architecture and community layout. And, the whole town is in a valley with I-70 running thru it! Utah is a far less progressive state than Colorado.

Once again, thank you for your time, energy, and consideration. I hope you get the best ski vacation any of us could ever manifest, with or without a stay in my home (((<3)))

host_about:
Hi! My name is Alexandre. I am a spirited and adventurous documentary filmmaker and comic book writer, originally from Geneva, Switzerland. My last three films -- "78/52: Hitchcock's Shower Scene" ; "Memory: The Origins of Alien" ; and "Leap of Faith: William Friedkin on The Exorcist" -- premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2017, 2019, and 2020, respectively. 78/52 is now available on Hulu and Blu Ray/DVD; and Memory is also available on Blu Ray/DVD and on most digital platforms. Leap of Faith is currently streaming on Shudder. My latest film, Lynch/Oz, just premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in June!

I'm currently working on several exciting feature projects, and always traveling as a result. This is why I choose to make my home available to fellow travelers. I am driven by mindfulness, integrity, kindness, empathy, childlike curiosity, an endless fascination for this extraordinary world we live in, and a passion for creative expression. 

If you like watching docs, you may have come across some of my other titles on Netflix or Hulu: The People vs. George Lucas, Doc of the Dead, The Life and Times of Paul the Psychic Octopus, etc. 

I have lived in Switzerland, France, England (Dorset, to be exact), Zimbabwe (Harare), San Diego, San Francisco, NYC (college years), and now Denver. I’m crazy about Northern California, the Pacific Northwest, and New Zealand... and will probably be visiting one of said places while you're enjoying my loft! ;)

I'm a huge movie buff, and my new loft has just been fully upgraded with a state-of-the-art LG C1 OLED 77" screen with Sonos sound bar! So you'll have your own mini movie theater right inside your home away from home!

Favorite filmmakers: David Lynch, William Wyler, Alfred Hitchcock, Mikio Naruse, Akira Kurosawa, Kiyoshi Kurosawa, Sergio Leone, Ingmar Bergman, Wes Anderson, Stanley Kubrick, David Lean, Orson Welles, John Huston, Josef von Sternberg, Michelangelo Antonioni, P.T. Anderson, Joel & Ethan Coen... okay, I'm going to stop here.

Films I couldn't do without: Vertigo, Strangers on a Train, Psycho, Mulholland Drive, Seven Samurai, Rushmore, Woman in the Dunes, The Shining, Citizen Kane, The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford, Blade Runner, Star Wars, The Big Sleep, The Killing, Nosferatu, Fargo, and... The Good, The Bad & The Ugly.
